title: Observability snowball: ingestion/trace/metrics debug logbook
content:
Context / tl;dr:
- Since 2025-11-01 we've seen stepwise degradation: trace sampling appears to drop ~40% for a subset of services, followed by log ingestion lag on the obs-ingest-kafka consumer and then a ~15% metric emission gap (prometheus scrape counts) across 3 clusters.
- This doc is my scratchbook: commands I ran, outputs, rough hypotheses, and next steps. Meant for quick handoff.

Timeline + notable events:
- 2025-11-01 03:14 UTC: first alert: trace coverage down (alert JIRA-OBS-782 triggered by sampling_rate_drop policy).
- 2025-11-02 13:00 UTC: observed consumer restarts for obs-ingest-consumer-0 in eu-west-1 (k8s restarts: 6x in 12h).
- 2025-11-03 08:21 UTC: metric gateway scrape misses logged on prod-metrics-gw (scrape timeout ~10s, default 5s).
- 2025-11-04 – ongoing: intermittent spike in kafka lag for topic obs-raw-1 (consumer group: obs-ingest-consumers).

Commands tried (copy/paste runnable):
- Check consumer group status:
  kafka-consumer-groups.sh --bootstrap-server kafka-obs.prod:9092 --describe --group obs-ingest-consumers
  -> shows partitions with LAG ~>100k for obs-ingest-consumer-0

- Tail recent logs from the pod that was repeatedly restarting:
  kubectl -n obs logs obs-ingest-consumer-0 -p --since=3h | sed -n '1,240p'
  snippets seen:
  "ERROR: UnhandledPromiseRejectionWarning: EOF while parsing frame"
  "WARN: consumer heartbeat timeout (session timed out)"
  "INFO: rebalancing triggered: group coordinator unreachable"

- Quick grep across last 72h of logs for 'sampling' and 'drop':
  kubectl -n obs logs --selector app=instrumentation -l env=prod --since=72h | grep -i "sampling\|drop" | tail -n 50
  -> many lines: "sampling rate changed from 1/10 to 1/100 for endpoint /api/v1/*" around 2025-11-01 03:10 UTC coming from tracing-proxy v1.12.3

- Check deployments for recent rollouts:
  kubectl -n obs rollout history deploy/tracing-proxy
  -> last rollout 2025-10-31 22:46 (image: tracing-proxy:v1.12.3) – matches timing.

- Confirm prom scrape errors:
  kubectl -n metrics logs prod-metrics-gw-0 --since=48h | grep -i timeout | head -n 20
  -> "WARN: scrape timeout exceeded for target service-metrics: 10.5s" (we expect 5s)

Raw error snippets (captured):
- "UnhandledPromiseRejectionWarning: EOF while parsing frame at KafkaJSProtocol.decode (node_modules/kafkajs/src/decoders.js:42:15)"
- "Consumer heartbeat not received; leaving group (coordinator tcp://10.0.32.7:9092)"
- "trace-sampler: forced-downscale: inferred high backpressure, reducing sampler to 0.01"
- "prom-scrape: client canceled request: context deadline exceeded"

Initial observations / hypotheses (ranked):
1) Rolling change in tracing-proxy (v1.12.3) introduced a race/latency in the agent that causes backpressure — agents reduce sampling to avoid overload (explains sampling drop). Tracing proxy errors then cascade to kafka; consumer sees malformed frames (EOF).
2) Kafka broker GC / network hiccup around coordinator caused rebalances -> consumer heartbeats missed -> lag accumulation. This explains restarts and rebalance logs.
3) Prom gateway timeouts are secondary effect: when ingestion backlog rises, downstream systems slow and scrape handlers block/respond slowly causing scrape timeout. Not primary cause but amplifies alerts.
4) Configuration mismatch: tracing-proxy and obs-ingest-consumer use different kafka client config (v0.11 vs v1.0), leading to unexpected frame decoding when tracing-proxy uses a newer compression/feature flag.

Quick tests to validate hypothesis 1 & 4:
- Rollback tracing-proxy to v1.12.2 in a canary namespace and see if sampling returns. Command run (dry-run first):
  kubectl -n obs set image deploy/tracing-proxy tracing-proxy=ghcr.io/redwood/tracing-proxy:v1.12.2 --record --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
- Run a focused producer stress test against obs-raw-1 to recreate malformed frames locally. Small node script used to publish a few thousand messages -> reproduces EOF in consumer logs when using new client flag "enable.idempotence=true" with tracing-proxy build.

Data points that do NOT match hypothesis 1 alone:
- Some pods with tracing-proxy v1.12.3 are fine (zero errors), suggesting env/traffic shape matters or a feature-flag gating.
- The EOF frame decoding error is only appearing when messages are > 64KB; smaller spans flow normally. That suggests fragmentation/large payload handling issue.

Important metrics / numbers observed:
- Trace sampling reduction: from 12% overall traces to 7.1% in affected services (~40% relative drop in sampled traces for that path).
- Kafka lag: partition 4: LAG 124,302 messages (consumer index obs-ingest-consumer-0).
- Consumer restarts: 6 restarts in last 12 hours for the pod obs-ingest-consumer-0.
- Prom scrape failure rate: 2.8% of scrapes failed last 24h (baseline 0.1%).

Things I want to dig into next / TODO checklist (prioritized):
- [ ] Reproduce locally with a trimmed dataset: create a producer with a mix of small and large spans to exercise fragmentation path. Confirm reproducer steps and attach logs. (Assigned to: me)
- [ ] Canary rollback tracing-proxy to v1.12.2 for a small subset of traffic (dev-green) and monitor sampling, kafka errors, and prom scrapes for 1h. (Assign Rina)
- [ ] Compare kafka client config between tracing-proxy v1.12.2 and v1.12.3: specifically broker API versions, compression, and max.request.size. (Miguel)
- [ ] Increase consumer session.timeout.ms by 50% temporarily to see if heartbeat drift reduces restarts; watch for increased rebalances. (SRE on-call)
- [ ] Export last 24h of large spans (>64KB) to s3 for offline analysis. Might be a serialization bug. (me)
- [ ] Postbrief on slack #obs-incident with a concise timeline + recommended rollback if canary proves.

Mitigations / quick-workarounds to try (low-friction first):
- Toggle a feature flag in tracing-proxy that disables oversized-span-batching (feature flag: "enable-span-batching") -> should reduce >64KB messages.
- Temporarily raise prom scrape timeout to 15s for prod-metrics-gw to suppress cascading alerts while we stabilize.
- Configure consumer to skip/blackhole messages larger than X bytes to avoid decoder EOF (risky but reduces churn).

Notes to self / stray thoughts:
- The "EOF while parsing frame" strongly suggests a mismatch in frame boundaries or compression indicator. If tracing-proxy switched to snappy/lz4 compression by default it could produce frames the downstream node kafkajs decoder can't handle if configured differently.
- Look at JVM/Kafka broker logs around 2025-11-01 03:10 for any "Connection reset by peer" or "Request completed with error" lines. Could be network flakiness between brokers and consumers.
- We should add a small integration test in CI that publishes >64KB spans to a kafka test harness and validates consumer decode. Catches this earlier.

Hand-off summary (if you pick this up):
- Start by checking canary rollback results (Rina) + reproducer artifacts in /tmp/obs-repro-20251103.tar.gz.
- If rollback clears errors: schedule a hotfix release and run a mitigation play to avoid churn (increase session timeout, tweak feature flag).
- If rollback does NOT clear: focus on broker/client protocol differences (compression/versions) and the large message path.

Relevant links / refs (quick):
- reproducer (local): ~/projects/obs-repro/produce-large-spans.js
- slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C0123ABC45/p1698734123456
- Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OBS/pages/CON-OBS-452

End of logbook entry for now. Will append results from canary rollback and reproducer here.

---
Personal signature: Asha (obs-pager, morning tea depleted)
